teams.heading: Jake White names Isoa Nasilasila captain for Italy rematch at Twickenham
teams.body: The lock leads a side with Caleb Muntz at fly-half and Terio Tamani at scrum-half, Jiuta Wainiqolo and Peniasi Dakuwaqa on the wings and Ponipate Loganimasi at full-back. Iosefo Masi and Vinaya Habosi pair up in midfield, while Kitione Salawa packs down at No. 8 alongside Elia Canakaivata and Mesake Vocevoce. Friday's 11th-place final is a second meeting inside a week: Fiji beat Italy 21-16 in Round 6, their only win in six.

teams.heading: Borthwick rests George Furbank and recalls Freddie Steward for All Blacks rematch
teams.body: George Furbank picked up a knock in last weekend's 37-12 win over New Zealand and was available, but Borthwick has opted for the more defensively minded Leicester man for Saturday's rematch. Steward missed the 23 last time. Tommy Freeman, withdrawn last week with a thigh issue, returns on the right wing with Will Joseph switching left. Greg Fisilau makes his first England start, at seven, and Luke Cowan-Dickie starts ahead of Jamie George at hooker.

teams.heading: Thomas Domingo says France can crack the Springbok scrum at Twickenham
teams.body: Former France loosehead Thomas Domingo, capped 36 times and now advising referees on scrum matters, insists the South Africans are as beatable as anyone ahead of Sunday's final. His answer to their heavy, dense pack is speed at the hit: concede the minimum centimetres before they settle, because once they start going forward, holding them burns energy. He judged the Bok tightheads close to pushing across while staying legal, and called the hooker's footwork crucial. France conceded nine scrum penalties against the Boks in Paris.

lead.why: Fresh France-focused take on the scrum, France's sorest area against the Boks, now that the Ramos and Gros return has already run.

teams.heading: Jacob Stockdale recalled on Ireland's left wing for Australia, replacing Mack Hansen
teams.body: Ulster form has earned the 30-year-old a 44th cap: three tries in as many games for the province this season. He sat out the wins over Argentina, Fiji and South Africa, and the fifth-place final against the Wallabies will be his first Test since July's Nations Championship victory over Japan. Hansen is not in the matchday 23. Stockdale is one of eight Ulster players in Andy Farrell's squad, with Robert Baloucoune retained on the right after his two tries against the Springboks.

lead.why: Stockdale's recall is the fresh selection angle, separate from the Beirne captaincy already run.

teams.heading: Quesada hands Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi first Test start, Niccolò Cannone to captain Italy
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has made five changes to the XV that lost 16-21 to Fiji in Udine for Friday's 11th-place final rematch at Twickenham. Opoku-Gyamfi, the Bath lock with four caps, starts for the first time in a back row with Manuel Zuliani and Ross Vintcent, while Federico Ruzza partners Cannone, who leads the side, in the second row. Paolo Garbisi returns at fly-half alongside Stephen Varney, Leonardo Marin and Mori pair up in midfield, and Tommaso Allan, Ange Capuozzo and Monty Ioane are retained in the back three.

teams.heading: BBC's Tom English urges Scotland to let Liam McConnell loose against Argentina
teams.body: Liam McConnell's hat-trick in the 67-5 rout of Japan has BBC Scotland's chief sports writer Tom English wanting more of him in the seventh-place final against the Pumas. English called him "fantastically promising" but was less taken with the team's discipline. Scotland gave up seven penalties in the first half against Japan, and he argues Gregor Townsend must privately be cursing a habit that cost them heavily against New Zealand only a few weeks ago.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy weighs first Wales start for Reuben Morgan-Williams against Japan
teams.body: Tomos Williams has been carrying an injury, WalesOnline reports, and if he is ruled out of Saturday's ninth-place final, Morgan-Williams starts after bench outings against New Zealand and Australia, with Che Hope moving to the bench. The pack could be reshuffled too: Ryan Elias is in line to start at hooker ahead of captain Dewi Lake, and James Botham, player of the match against the All Blacks, is expected back after missing the narrow defeat to the Wallabies.

teams.heading: Matera and Sclavi HIAs caused eight-minute Pumas muddle in 45-17 loss
teams.body: With last Saturday's 45-17 defeat by France long decided, the Stade de France sat through nearly eight minutes of confusion at a 77th-minute French scrum. Pablo Matera had landed badly at an Argentine lineout and played on until a Pumas knock-on. With Julián Montoya sin-binned and unable to scrum, the staff sent on replacement hooker Facundo Bosch — just as Hollie Davidson signalled that Matera and Joel Sclavi both had to leave for head injury assessments. Davidson had to come to the touchline to make sense of the officials' instructions.

lead.why: The squad changes and the Brousset appointment have already run, so the strongest unread Argentina event is the 77th-minute replacement muddle in Paris.

teams.heading: Allan Alaalatoa named for 100th Wallabies Test and co-captaincy against Ireland
teams.body: The Brumbies tighthead becomes the 14th member of the Wallabies' centurion club at Twickenham on Friday, and his teammates gave him a two-minute ovation when the side was announced. "His was the first name we put up when we named the team, and the whole room erupted," said Les Kiss. The 32-year-old leads Australia out as co-captain for the day in their final Test of 2026, and Kiss said people in the squad don't want to let him down.

teams.heading: Japan draw Wales again in ninth-place final after losing round-four meeting 28-21
teams.body: Saturday's play-off at Twickenham will be the sides' second meeting inside three weeks, Wales having won the round-four encounter 28-21. Both finished fifth in their pools, by very different routes. Japan's only win came against Italy, 27-10 on 4 July, and they arrive having been beaten 78-15 by England and 67-5 by Scotland. Steve Tandy's Wales won three of six, ending 73 years without a win over New Zealand, and went close against Australia last weekend.

lead.why: It is the only new item, and it frames the ninth-place final as a quick Wales rematch for Japan.

teams.heading: Jordie Barrett rejects Graham Henry's fatigue theory before England rematch at Twickenham
teams.body: Henry, the former head coach now on the selection panel, said recently the side were tired after the Springbok series, but the inside centre wants none of it before Saturday's third-place play-off: "They're just inconvenient facts, but we're not going to use any excuse language this week. We need to be better." Barrett, nominated this week for World Rugby Player of the Year, called this probably the most difficult period of his All Blacks career and admitted to a knot in his gut over the team's form.

teams.heading: World Rugby reportedly investigating Rassie Erasmus watch-along and Mzwandile Stick's Prendergast comments
teams.body: Rassie, already banned for suggesting "match-fixing" after the Paris defeat, hosted an online watch-along of the Ireland loss from his Dublin hotel room and was seen speaking into a phone several times. Stick, on the eve of that Test, questioned whether Sam Prendergast would have been cleared over a hip-drop had he been Fijian: "But it's an Irish player, it's free to play." Nations Championship organisers have asked World Rugby whether those comments fall under its match officials abuse process or count as misconduct.

lead.why: A fresh disciplinary event involving the Springbok head coach and an assistant before the final; the Du Toit injury has already run.
